purpose: dual-netspeed 第一次實跑的 C 段 (design.md 第7節: B 段成功才跑這段) -- the full flow, identical create->join->ready->battle segment to experiments/dual-netspeed.json (kept there unchanged as the pre-split reference, same reorder applied to both), just split out under its own id/max_wall_clock_s per the PM's 2026-09-21 三段 decision: host (copy install, MetalRage2, account mrotesthost, patched IpDrv.dll MaxClientRate/MaxInternetClientRate=100000) launches and logs in; joiner (main install, MetalRage, account mrotest) launches and logs in, staying in the lobby with the room list open; focus_client(host) + create_pve_room (existing single-client action, room name is whatever the client auto-assigns -- this action has no room-naming field, so join_room's room_name param below is a traceability LABEL only, never matched on screen, see actions.py's join_room() docstring); join_room(joiner) (double-click the one visible room row, see actions.py's ROOM_LIST_FIRST_ROW_CLICK); set_ready(joiner); host_start_battle(); enter_battle(joiner) (no click -- mech-select is automatic, see actions.py's CHANGE_SLOT_CN_OPCODE comment); console_cmd_on(joiner, 'netspeed 100000'); a 5s settle; console_cmd_on(joiner, 'stat net'); leave_battle for both; close_client for both (flushes each instance's data/System/run-*.log). REVISED 2026-09-21 after B段's actual first run (which shares this same create->join->ready prefix and hit two failures there -- see experiments/dual-netspeed-b.json's purpose for the full incident: a bad ROOM_LIST_FIRST_ROW_CLICK, and the room's own AFK self-kick firing at 60,022ms measured, well before design.md L5's ~80s estimate, because idle_nudge(host) ran only once, AFTER join_room). Same two fixes applied here: ROOM_LIST_FIRST_ROW_CLICK corrected and DEFAULT_JOIN_ROOM_TIMEOUT_S lowered 45->20 in actions.py (shared by every script, not just B段); idle_nudge(host) moved to right after create_pve_room PLUS a second one added right after join_room, splitting the host's no-input span into three windows each kept under the measured 60s ceiling by summing actions.py's own timeout constants (focus_client switches assumed ~5s, this budget's one non-constant, flagged as residual risk -- see dual-netspeed-b.json's purpose for why): window A (Create_CQ -> idle_nudge#1) ~16s (create_pve_room confirm ceiling 10s + focus ~5s + wiggle); window B (idle_nudge#1 -> idle_nudge#2, spans join_room) ~43s (focus ~5s + precondition ~2s + Enter_SA wait ceiling 20s + join_room-room wait ceiling 10s + focus back ~5s + wiggle); window C (idle_nudge#2 -> host_start_battle's own F5 send, a deliberate host input, not an AFK boundary) ~35s (focus to joiner ~5s + set_ready precondition ~2s + User_State_SN wait ceiling 20s + result screenshot ~1s + focus to host ~5s + host_start_battle precondition ~2s) -- all three comfortably under 60s (margins 44s/17s/25s). Success = result PASS, with host_start_battle's Game_Start_SN send pkt and enter_battle's ChangeSlot_CN/Respawn_CN recv pkt both conn-filtered and present, plus both console_cmd_on screenshots saved. Reading the host's run-*.log for 'Client netspeed is N' afterward (design.md section 7 step 10) is a manual/analysis step done AFTER this script exits, not a runner action -- it needs no Pico/client/server interaction. If it halts, look first at join_room (ROOM_LIST_FIRST_ROW_CLICK is re-measured but still click-UNCONFIRMED, see actions.py's comment on that constant), then at host_start_battle (design.md L1: only the conn-filtered Game_Start_SN pkt counts, not the gameStarted_ text marker) and at enter_battle (design.md L6: the joiner's mech-select page has to resolve on its own with no click sent).
